title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A field K (characteristic 0, as fixed on the previous page) is attached to three equivalent 'Galois' invariants:
- its étale topos B_K, the classifying topos of the profinite Galois group;
- its fundamental groupoid Π_K;
- for a choice of separable closure K̄, the Galois group E_{K̄/K}.
The previous page analysed the map E_{K̄'/K'} → E_{K̄/K} (its (3)) induced by an extension K → K'. Its image has finite index, with K_1 = K̄ ∩ K' as the relative algebraic closure. It is injective iff K'/K is algebraic. It is bijective iff K'/K is radicial, which in characteristic 0 means K → K' is an isomorphism. So the 2-functor K ↦ B_K ≃ Π_K ≃ E_{K̄/K} is conservative on finite-type extensions.

This page, first part. A convenient instance is the category of fields of finite type over the prime field Q. There every morphism K → K' between such fields is automatically of finite type. One therefore gets a functor from this category to groupoids (or to topoi) that is conservative: a field morphism inducing an equivalence of groupoids (or of topoi) is an isomorphism.

Diagonal margin addition. As far as it can be read, it strengthens this to a conjecture: a field of finite type over Q is determined up to isomorphism by its Galois category (finite étale extensions, i.e. B_K or Π_K), and the functor K ↦ B_K or Π_K should even be fully faithful. This is the birational (field-theoretic) anabelian conjecture.

This page, second part. For arbitrary fields the 2-functor is far from faithful. If K is separably closed, B_K is the punctual topos, Π_K the punctual groupoid and E = 1, so morphisms between separably closed fields are invisible.

The remedy, continued on the next page. Replace B_K by the pro-system (B_{K_i}) indexed by the finitely generated subfields K_i of K, and similarly for Π and E. One cannot recover B_K as the projective limit (the next page says the naive limit formula is false). But Ind(fields of finite type) → Fields is an equivalence. Hence an anabelian full faithfulness for finitely generated fields would formally extend to a full faithfulness of K ↦ 'pro-system of Galois data of f.g. subfields'.

Purpose. This sets up the anabelian programme at the level of fields (the 'birational' part of the Longue Marche / letter to Faltings). It also identifies the right invariant for fields that are not finitely generated.
errors: If the margin indeed asserts full faithfulness without restriction, it is too strong as stated. A non-algebraic finite-type extension K → K' induces a homomorphism of Galois groups whose image has finite index but which is not injective. Conversely, not every homomorphism of Galois groups comes from a field map. The correct 'Hom-form' (Mochizuki 1999 for sub-p-adic fields; Pop for Isom-form) restricts to open homomorphisms taken modulo inner automorphisms. Grothendieck himself adds such restrictions in the letter to Faltings.

The conservativity statement is correct only in characteristic 0, or up to radicial extensions in characteristic p (e.g. Frobenius induces an equivalence). This caveat was made on the previous page, so it is not an error on this page, just a dependency.

Minor: the main text says 'functor ... into groupoids'. Strictly this is a 2-functor, and full faithfulness must be understood on Hom-sets of isomorphism classes of functors, i.e. outer homomorphisms.

ideas.what: Conservativity of K ↦ Galois group / étale topos / fundamental groupoid on finite-type extensions in char 0 (a morphism inducing an equivalence is an isomorphism)
ideas.modern_name: Elementary Galois-theoretic conservativity (injectivity iff algebraic, bijectivity iff radicial)

ideas.what: A field finitely generated over Q is determined (up to isomorphism) by its Galois category; the functor to groupoids/topoi should be fully faithful
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984, letter to Faltings 1983); proved by Neukirch–Uchida (number fields), Pop (1994, f.g. fields; Isom-form), Mochizuki (1999, Hom-form over sub-p-adic fields)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984); La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Failure of faithfulness for arbitrary fields (separably closed fields give the punctual topos)
ideas.modern_name: Need for finiteness hypotheses in anabelian geometry

ideas.what: Replace B_K by the pro-system of B_{K_i} over finitely generated subfields K_i; use Ind(f.t. fields) ≃ Fields to extend anabelian full faithfulness formally to all fields
ideas.modern_name: Pro-/Ind-extension of the anabelian functor to arbitrary fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: not standardly credited; arbitrary fields are usually handled instead via Bogomolov–Pop-style results over algebraically closed bases

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes attaching to an arbitrary field K the pro-system of Galois topoi of its finitely generated subfields as the correct anabelian invariant. He notes that the 'birational anabelian' full faithfulness would then extend formally to all fields via Ind(f.t. fields) ≃ Fields. This is a formal reformulation rather than a new theorem, but this particular packaging is not a standard formulation in the literature.
missed.quote: il y a lieu d'associer à un corps K un objet plus fin que B_K ou Π_K, à savoir le système projectif des B_{K_i}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean categorical statement of anabelian reconstruction for arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed or infinitely generated) fields as a corollary of Pop–Mochizuki. It contrasts with the Bogomolov–Pop approach, which uses pro-ℓ abelian-by-central quotients over an algebraically closed base. This is of modest expository interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states the birational anabelian conjecture (well known and credited to Grothendieck) and an elementary conservativity result. The pro-system device for arbitrary fields is a natural formal remark rather than a substantive missed result.
transcription_corrections: In line 4 the word before 'de la cat.' appears in the image to end in '...tif'. It is likely 'conservatif', consistent with the previous page's 'conservatif', rather than an inserted 'pleinement fidèle'. The 'pleinement fidèle' idea seems to belong to the diagonal margin note.
'(ou des topos)' is inserted above 'groupoïdes', i.e. 'celle des groupoïdes (ou des topos), au sens :'.
'(K,K̄) → E_{K̄/K}' is written above the line, as 'ou (K,K̄) ↦ E_{K̄/K} est cependant loin d'être fidèle'.

The diagonal margin note is largely illegible. Readable fragments suggest '... un corps de type fini ... est connu ... par la catégorie ... des extensions ... (le foncteur K ↦ B_K ou Π_K ... pleinement fidèle ...)'. Treat this as a tentative reading.
